Engine source & fidelity

The GitHub F136 F engine file describes a community Engine-Sim configuration for the 458, not a 3D engine assembly. Its 9,000 rpm redline informs this display; no source code is copied or executed. The repository itself labels some piston parameters as guesses.

Original engine geometry is not included. Ignition and accelerator drive an illustrative RPM response; brake activates the modeled rear light surfaces. Headlights illuminate the source light surfaces. Driving mode provides arcade acceleration, braking, reverse and steering with a following camera. Controls also work by keyboard or touch. The headlight ground patch and lamp brightness are illustrative; no measured beam optics, factory ECU logic or validated driving physics are simulated. Horn audio is synthesized, not recorded from a Ferrari. The original 3D engine assembly remains unavailable.

Model details & credits

Ferrari 458 Italia visual model by vicent091036, distributed with the official three.js car example under CC BY 4.0 (repository license record). Adaptation: source meshes have been separated into 1030 connected geometric pieces, preserving all 3,58,788 triangles. No screws or internal mechanisms have been invented. The source's four “nuts” meshes contain 24 separate fastener mesh pieces, which are individually removable here. A connected piece is not necessarily one manufacturing part; decorative surfaces also count.

Visual model · not engineering CAD. The source is an artist's visual model of a real Ferrari, not scanned or factory-verified assembly CAD. It does not include every engine/chassis screw, internal piston, thread, or hidden mechanism. Source labels are preserved; mesh IDs are viewer IDs, not Ferrari part numbers. Removal order, spin, and offsets are illustrative—not a workshop procedure or validated mechanical simulation. Materials are restyled; source textures are not reproduced. Display coordinates use 0.1 mm quantization.

＋ removes one piece at the selected step size. − restores the last removed unit along the reverse animation. Reassemble resets all pieces. The lower-right preview shows the most recently moved unit; orbiting also rotates that preview. To inspect just a nut: search “fastener”, select it, then use Isolate selection. Download mesh-piece index. Model attribution: vicent091036; independent viewer with no Ferrari affiliation.
